claims.claim_text: Americans are justly proud of the U.S. armed forces.
In 2000, nine years after victory in the Persian Gulf War, the U.S. military faces growing problems with readiness, morale and preparation for future threats.
The U.S. administration in office in 2000 has cut defense spending to its lowest share of U.S. gross domestic product since before Pearl Harbor.
The U.S. administration in office in 2000 has sent American armed forces on dozens of missions without clear goals, realizable objectives, favorable rules of engagement or defined exit strategies.
The strength of the U.S. military lies in its combat soldiers, sailors, airmen and Marines.
